statement: The functions $f$ and $g$ are defined by $f(x) = x^2 - 3x$ and $g(x) = 2x + 1$. What is the value of $f(g(2))$?

choices.misconception: I multiplied $f(2) = -2$ by $g(2) = 5$ instead of putting $g(2)$ into $f$.
I found $f(2) = -2$ first and then $g(-2) = -3$, which is $g(f(2))$, not $f(g(2))$.
I added $f(2) = -2$ and $g(2) = 5$ instead of putting one function inside the other.

hints: Work from the inside out: start with $g(2)$.
Find $g(2)$, then use that number as the input to $f$.
